pinterest.title: When to Marry in Mauritius: Seasons, Sunshine and Your Coast
pinterest.description: Mauritius has a mild tropical maritime climate with two seasons. Summer, November to April, is warm and humid. Winter, June to September, is relatively cool and dry, with October and May as transition months. Cyclone season runs from November to May. Coastal areas see more bright sunshine than the high ground, so the coast you choose shapes the light you marry in. Read the full Mauritius wedding guide.

slides: Planning a Mauritius wedding? Here is the legal sequence for Australian couples, step by step.
Two Australians marry through the Civil Status Division's civil process for two non-citizens, celebrated by a Civil Status Officer.
Step 1: Send your documents to the Central Civil Status Office in Port Louis 6 to 8 weeks before the wedding. The application must arrive at least one month ahead.

What to send: a coversheet, two photocopies of each birth certificate (English or French, issued within 3 months), two photocopies of each passport, plus any divorce, widowhood or name change documents.
Step 2: When you land, visit the Office together so it can verify your original documents. It then issues a Certificate of Authority.
Step 3: After a 24-hour publication, a Civil Status Officer celebrates the marriage, at the Office, a marriage hall, a hotel or other premises. Two witnesses must be present.
Back home: Australia generally recognises a marriage that was valid where it took place. Keep your original certificate safe in case you need an Apostille.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Mauritius is on the shortlist. Here is how the legal side works for Australian couples.

1. Send your documents to the Central Civil Status Office in Port Louis 6 to 8 weeks before the wedding. Your application must reach the Office at least one month ahead.
2. When you land, visit the Office together with your original documents so they can be verified. The Office then issues a Certificate of Authority.
3. After a 24-hour publication, a Civil Status Officer celebrates your marriage. It can be held at the Office, a marriage hall, a hotel or other premises, with two witnesses present.

Birth certificates must be in English or French and issued not more than 3 months earlier, so order fresh copies once your date is fixed.

Australia generally recognises a marriage that was valid where it took place. Keep your original marriage certificate safe, because only originals (or copies certified by a notary and the Supreme Court) can take an Apostille.

Thinking about the season? Summer, November to April, is warm and humid. Winter, June to September, is relatively cool and dry.

newsletter.subject: Planning a Mauritius wedding: the legal steps in order
newsletter.preview: Documents, Port Louis, a 24-hour publication and the ceremony: the sequence for Australian couples.
newsletter.blurb: Mauritius on your list? Our new guide sets out the legal sequence for Australian couples: documents to the Central Civil Status Office in Port Louis 6 to 8 weeks ahead, a visit together with your originals when you land, a 24-hour publication, then a civil ceremony before a Civil Status Officer with two witnesses. It covers the documents to send, how your marriage is recognised at home, Apostilles, the seasons and choosing your coast.
